summary.text: In calculus, a linear function is a function whose graph is a straight line: a polynomial of degree zero or one.
Written with two constants, one is the slope of the line and the other the intercept.
In linear algebra the term is stricter, so the calculus kind is often called an affine function instead.

facts.label: Slope sign
facts.value: Positive slopes upward, negative slopes downward

facts.label: Constant function
facts.value: Counts as linear in calculus; its graph is horizontal

facts.label: Linear map test
facts.value: The graph must pass through the origin

facts.label: Intercept
facts.value: The constant b is the intercept

items.prompt: A linear function's graph slopes downward as you move to the right. What is true of its slope?

options.label: It is negative
It is positive
It is zero
It is undefined

items.explain: If a < 0, the slope is negative and the graph slopes downwards.

items.prompt: A taxi charges a flat fee, whatever the distance. In the calculus sense, is that fee as a function of distance linear?

options.label: Yes, its graph is a horizontal line
No, its graph must slope
No, it has no variable
Only when the fee is positive

items.explain: A constant function is a polynomial of degree zero, so it is linear in this context, with a horizontal graph.

items.prompt: A line drawn straight up and down on graph paper: can it be the graph of a one-variable linear function?

options.label: Yes, with a very large slope
No, such a graph is never vertical
Yes, if the intercept is zero
Yes, if it passes through the origin

items.explain: The graph of a linear function of one variable is a nonvertical line.

items.prompt: A function doubles its input and then adds 3. Its graph is a straight line. In the linear algebra sense, is it a linear map?

options.label: Yes, because its graph is a line
Yes, because the slope is positive
No, because its graph misses the origin
No, because it is constant

items.explain: A calculus linear function is a linear map only when the constant is zero, so the graph must pass through the origin.

items.prompt: A textbook wants a name for any function with a straight-line graph, avoiding the clash with linear algebra's stricter meaning. Which?

options.label: Constant function
Linear form
Homogeneous function
Affine function

items.explain: To avoid confusion, functions with an arbitrary line as graph are often called affine functions.

items.prompt: In linear algebra, which test must a function pass to count as linear?

options.label: It preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication
Its graph has a positive slope
It is a polynomial of degree exactly two
It never takes the value zero

items.explain: In linear algebra, a linear function preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication.
